title: Between the Cheats Season 3 Is Coming to Tubi
subtitle: When infidelity ends in murder, the receipts are all real.
intro:
True crime has covered every angle of the human capacity for violence, but Between the Cheats zeroes in on something most of us already know is dangerous: the moment trust dies. This series isn't interested in fictional drama. It pulls from actual police footage, real testimony, and the people who were standing closest when everything collapsed.

There's something about infidelity-driven crime that cuts through the noise right now. We're in a moment where everyone has an opinion about loyalty, betrayal, and what people are capable of when they feel wronged. Between the Cheats doesn't theorize about it. It shows you.

Each episode is its own contained gut punch. A relationship fractures, someone makes an irreversible decision, and the cameras and courts caught all of it. This is the kind of true crime that doesn't let you keep a comfortable distance.

items.name: Jesse Weber
items.bio: Weber is a legal analyst who knows how to translate courtroom complexity into something a real person can follow. He brings credibility and pace to the storytelling here, keeping the legal threads tight without losing the human weight underneath each case.

items.name: Elizabeth Millner
items.bio: Millner grounds the series in the emotional reality of each story. She has a way of holding space for the people who survived these cases without letting the narrative tip into exploitation. That balance is harder to pull off than it looks.

quote: You thought it was just a lie. It was a fuse.

whyWatch.body: Between the Cheats works because it never has to invent stakes. The stakes were already there, already documented, already adjudicated. The real police footage isn't a gimmick. It's evidence. And watching the series, you feel the weight of that word in a way that dramatized crime shows rarely achieve.
